The right-hand page of a book is called the recto. It's where the eye lands first, so it's where printers put what matters. That's the whole idea behind the name.
Before you hit send: five things every proposal needs, in this order.

1. Their problem, in their words. Proof you listened.
2. What you'll do. Scope, not adjectives.
3. When. A timeline with real dates.

4. What it costs and how it's paid. Deposit, milestones, done.
5. What happens next. One clear step.
Everything else is decoration. Make the decoration good, but never let it replace these five.

text: English left to right, Kurdish or Arabic right to left, on the same page, each one looking like it belongs. Recto has Arabic and Kurdish faces among its 60+ fonts, and warns you when a font can't show a Kurdish letter.
Kurdish has letters many Arabic-script fonts were never drawn for: ڕ ڵ ێ ۆ ە. If a font can't set them, it isn't ready for Kurdish, however beautiful it looks.
